title: optimized compiling for general QubitExcitations beyond single and double
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The `QubitExcitation` gate in tequila supports optimized decompositions for single and double qubit excitation operations. But triple and higher resort to the standard Pauli decomposition. Now the circuits scale with the number of Pauli strings and are quite expensive. 

Here is some example code. You will need
```bash
pip install tequila-basic
```

```python
import tequila as tq

# Here comes a double excitation (between qubits 0,1 and 2,3
# does operations like: |111000> --> cos(a)|1100> -sin(a)|0011> 
circuit = tq.gates.QubitExcitation(angle="a", target=[0,1,2,3])

# compiling into Pauli-Gates 
decomposition1 = tq.compile_circuit(circuit, exponential_pauli=False)
# compiling into CNOT, Rx, Ry, Rz and (multi-)controlled versions
# this is what the optimized compiling scheme does
decomposition2 = tq.compile_circuit(circuit, controlled_rotation=False, cc_max=False, multicontrol=False)
# compiling into CNOT, Rx, Ry, Rz
decomposition3 = tq.compile_circuit(circuit)

# non-optimized decomposition (standard Pauli compilation)
circuit = tq.gates.QubitExcitation(angle="a", target=[0,1,2,3], compile_options="pauli")
decomposition4 = tq.compile_circuit(circuit)

print("\n\n")
print("optimized compiling to CNOT and Rxyz: ", decomposition3.depth)
print("default compiling to CNOT and Rxyz: ", decomposition4.depth)
print("\n\n")

# Here comes a triple excitation (between qubits 0,1,2 and 3,4,5
# does operations like: |111000> --> cos(a)|111000> -sin(a)|000111> 
circuit = tq.gates.QubitExcitation(angle="a", target=[0,1,2,3,4,5])

decomposition1 = tq.compile_circuit(circuit, exponential_pauli=False)
decomposition2 = tq.compile_circuit(circuit, controlled_rotation=False, cc_max=False, multicontrol=False)
decomposition3 = tq.compile_circuit(circuit)

# non-optimized decomposition (standard Pauli compilation)
circuit = tq.gates.QubitExcitation(angle="a", target=[0,1,2,3,4,5], compile_options="pauli")
decomposition4 = tq.compile_circuit(circuit)

print("\n\n")
print("at this point no difference")
print("optimized compiling to CNOT and Rxyz: ", decomposition3.depth)
print("default compiling to CNOT and Rxyz: ", decomposition4.depth)
print("\n\n")

```

If you want to draw the circuits you can use
```python
circuit.export_to("file.pdf")
```
In order to be able to get the circuits as pdf you need
```bash
pip install qpic
```
as well as a working `pdflatex` command. 
Alternatively you can export the circuits to `cirq`, or `qiskit` via

```python
compiled_circuit = tq.compile(circuit, backend="qiskit")
qiskit_circuit = compiled_circuit.circuit
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
In the source file for [gates](https://github.com/tequilahub/tequila/blob/master/src/tequila/circuit/gates.py), there is the class `QubitExcitationImpl`, here the function `compile` is checking if `n=2 or n=4` to realize optimized decompositions. The number `n` is the number of qubits onto which the gate acts (for a single excitations these are 2 qubits, for an $N$-fold excitation we will have `n=2N` qubits. 
Ideally this `compile` function is extended to perform the optimized decomposition for *any* `n`. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
But manual solutions for `n=6` and/or `n=8` are also welcome. 

**Additional context**
more information can be found in this [talk](https://kottmanj.github.io/talks_and_material/qai2022/talk.pdf) where the compilation of the QubitExcitations is described. 

For `FermionicExcitations` tequila already supports more general compiling schemes. The strategy is basically the same. You can find the implementation in [quantumchemistry/chemistry_tools.py](https://github.com/tequilahub/tequila/blob/master/src/tequila/quantumchemistry/chemistry_tools.py) where the class `FermionicGateImpl` resembles the `QubitExcitation` class -- the Fermionic version just as additional `Z` operations in the defining PauliStrings.
